name: Siphon
description: Bring Stremio catalogs, metadata, subtitles and stream versions to native Jellyfin libraries.

versions.changelog: Reuse the successful native media classification attached to an authorized proxy lease for later large seek requests. Avoid repeated byte-zero classification reads that can stall after an origin has already accepted the requested range, while retaining range validation, representation validator checks, HLS rewriting, exact source identity and fail-closed behavior. Add regressions proving that large seeks skip the redundant classification request and still reject changed representations. Verified with 586 tests and the complete owned Jellyfin integration workflow.

Preserve the exact opened native source for Jellyfin remux, HLS and seek requests after discovery withdrawal by binding a private source snapshot to the user, PlaySessionId and native version. Reuse the already-authorized opaque proxy lease, revalidate permissions, ownership, content and session identity, and fail closed without substituting another version. Add controlled Jellyfin 12.1 coverage for progressive and nested HLS playback, seeking, decoded audio/video and playback revocation. Verified with 584 tests and the complete owned Jellyfin smoke workflow.

Avoid overlapping classification and media responses within a playback relay request. Classify long byte-zero reads in place and finish prefix classification before seeks or short ranges. Preserve HLS rewriting, exact source selection, authorization and SSRF safeguards; reject conflicting advertised representations and invalid ranges. Add credential-free stage and cause diagnostics for relay failures. Verified with 578 tests and real Jellyfin playback, including bounded reads at 6 GiB and generated HEVC/AAC seeking. Independent FFmpeg requests can still overlap; the reported production NAS failure is not yet verified resolved.

Route native FFmpeg and ffprobe reads through Jellyfin's bound local HTTP address and port instead of the public reverse proxy, while preserving public playback URLs for clients. Keep rewritten HLS playlists, segments and keys on the reader's origin and base path. Avoid reopening and probing an already-probed selected version during remux and seek. Preserve capability authorization, account isolation, range validation and private-host safeguards. Includes regression and real Jellyfin coverage with an unreachable public playback hostname.

Identify failed catalog subscriptions in Tasks and synchronization history with stable identities and safe causes, persisted across restarts without exposing credentials or upstream errors. Partial synchronization still reports Failed and preserves prior media. Fix equivalent GUID handling and keep non-playable metadata available for canonical and retired versions so native progress/stop reports can save resume state without reopening retired sources or crossing user boundaries. Adds English/French failure details and regression coverage for catalog preservation, safe persistence and playback reporting.

Fix a Jellyfin startup regression when an existing Siphon catalog exceeds 256 MiB. Large valid state files load and save without truncation, preserving native identities, ownership and metadata; the 100,000-item limit and atomic writes remain enforced. Prevent calendar notification starvation under brief publication-lock contention and create generated native collections with their initial members, preserving manual additions. Correct native login and notification smoke synchronization, allow matching source/catalog versions after publication, update the Node.js action runtime, and pin Linux CI to Ubuntu 24.04. Detailed release notes now come from annotated tags rather than a tracked notes file.

Siphon 1.5.0.0: private user addon profiles, native collections and saved additions, selected-version HTTP/P2P downloads, source and metadata diagnostics, selective history recovery, followed-series calendar and opt-in notifications, targeted synchronization, provider quotas and shared caching, IntroDB timings, and bounded opt-in P2P playback. Includes media-response validation and the unchanged supplied icon. Persistent offline queues, offline HLS exports and external webhooks remain unreleased 1.6 features.
